full_judgment:
2. Short facts, for the disposal of this petition, are that the present petitioners filed Title Suit No.04 of 2008 in the Second Court of Joint District Judge, Barguna for declaration that the judgment and decree dated 28.11.2002 passed in Title Suit No.15 of 1995 was fraudulent, void, inoperative and the same was not binding upon the plaintiffs. The defendant Nos.1-12 contested the said suit by filing written statement. The trial Court, by its judgment and decree dated 27.09.2016, dismissed the suit. The plaintiff-petitioners filed Title Appeal No.17 of 2017 in the Court of District Judge, Barguna which was dis-missed by a judgment and decree dated 23.01.2008. Then the plaintiff-petitioners filed a civil revisional application in the High Court Division and obtained Rule. In the High Court Division, the plaintiff-petitioners filed an application for withdrawal of the suit with a permission to sue afresh. The High Court Division by the impugned order observed that the application for withdrawal is misconceived, malafide, ill advised and motivated. But finally it allowed an option .to the plaintiffs to file a fresh suit in accordance with law by the impugned order dated 01.02.2021. 

 4. Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioners, submits that there was formal defect in initiating the instant suit, the High Court Division erred in law in not giving permission to withdraw the suit and to file a suit afresh. He further submits that the learned Judge-in-Chamber directed the parties to maintain status-quo in respect of possession of the suit land but the respondents, violating the order of status-quo, dispossessed the plaintiff-petitioners from the suit land. On the other hand, Mr. Asaduzzaman, learned Counsel appearing for the respondents submits that earlier Mofiz Mridha, predecessor-in-interest of the present respondents and some other respondents, instituted Title Suit No.15 of 1995 for partition against the predecessor-in-interest of the some of the present petitioners and others. Which was dismissed by the trial Court by a judgment and decree dated 28.11.2002. Against which, the present respondents, who were the plaintiffs in earlier suit, preferred Title Appeal No.11 of 2003 in the Court of District Judge, Barguna and the said appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, Barguna who, by a judgment and decree dated 30.09.2007, allowed the appeal and decreed the suit upon setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court and allotted saham in favour of the present respondents to the extent of 10.81 acres of land. Thereafter, the present petitioners instituted Title Suit No.04 of 2008 for setting aside the aforesaid decree which was dismissed by the trial Court holding that the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.15 of 1995 was reversed by the appellate Court and that the Joint District Judge, Second Court, Barguna is not authorized to set aside the appellate decree passed in Title Appeal No.11 of 2003. Against the said judgment and decree of the trial Court in Title Suit No.04 of 2008, the plaintiff-petitioners unsuccessfully preferred Title Appeal No.17 of 2017 and, thereafter, obtained Rule from the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.715 of 2018. In the said civil revision, the plaintiff-petitioners filed application for withdrawal of the suit. The High Court Division though observed that the application for withdrawal of the suit at this belated stage was misconceived, malafide, ill advised and motivated one but finally, allowed the plaintiff-petitioners to file a fresh suit in accordance with law if they so desire. The operating portion of the judgment is inconsistent with the earlier observation of the High Court Division that the application for withdrawal was misconceived, malafide, ill advised and motivated one. 

 5. We have perused the application for withdrawal. In the said application, we do not find anything about the nature of alleged formal defect in the said suit. The present respondents obtained a contested decree in Title Appeal No.11 of 2003 for partition to the extent of 10.81 acres of land in preliminary form. But due to the present suit, appeal and revision, they could not proceed with the said suit for making preliminary decree final. A mere statement by the plaintiff-petitioners that there are formal defects in the frame and form of suit is not enough. There must be an express statement by the plaintiffs that suit would fail by reason, of some formal defect or that there are other sufficient reasons for granting the leave to file a fresh suit. The High Court, in revision, should be slow and cautious to exercise the powers under Order XXIII Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure and permit the defeated plaintiffs to withdraw the suit with liberty to file fresh suit so as to enable him to reagitate the matter once again. We have gone through the plaintiffs' case and the judgments of the Courts below and revisional application. The Rule does not have any merit so the same is liable to be discharged.
